text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Chancellor Viktor Klima does not rule out the possibility of a parliamentary committee to investigate Iranian intervention and the government's involvement in the prosecution of the murderers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989. Former foreign minister Alois Mock says current President Thomas Klestil also knew of Iran's intervention, even though he had denied it.

- A tarriffs reform by telecommunications monopoly Post & Telekom Austria could save clients up to 3.3 billion schillings in phone costs. Local calls will see a huge price hike while long distance calls will become cheaper.

- Economic research institute Wifo criticises federal railways OeBB for its low prices especially in local transport compared to Switzerland and Germany, leading to the majority of its earnings coming from state subsidies.
- Klima and the civil servants union boss Siegfried Dohr have talked about reducing privileges of civil servants in order to reduce costs.

- Salzburg's conservative state leader Franz Schausberger demands Social Democrats support President Thomas Klestil for a second term as president in 1998. He expects vice-chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel to remain the party's leader at the next general election in 1999.
- The committee to reform Austria's tax system by the year 2000 should make the country's investment preference conform to European Union laws.
- The European Union's European Investment Bank has paid out nearly 10 billion schillings in credits for projects in Austria since the country became a member of the EU.

- "We will do everything to fulfil the convergence criteria in time" said German Finance Minister Theo Waigel in an interview, adding he stands for a strict interpretation of the Maastricht criteria for the European Economic and Monetary Union.
- Austria's top ski jumper and former world champion Andreas Goldberger has been excluded from the Austrian national team after he admitted having tried cocaine once.

- Insurer Wiener Staedtische's boss Siegfried Sellitsch wants the postal service and postal savings bank PSK to work together more closely. Talks about a participation of his company in PSK have been denied so far.
- The abolition of Austria's anonymous savings accounts will be decided by the European Commission in the near future. The final decision, however, will be handed to the European Court of Justice.
- The first company to be listed with the Vienna stock exchange's fit-programme for middle-sized firms will be ready before the summer. Banks criticise the high trading fees for investors.
- Regional utility firm EVN has raised its bid for regional gas provider Begas to 400 million schillings. Oil and chemicals group OMV is now seen to have little chance in winning the bid.
- Science Minister Caspar Einem wants earnings from privatisations to be spent more on subsidising research and development.
